translation: As for thirst from intestinal bi (腸痹), one drinks frequently yet cannot retain it within; the qi is panting and struggling. (The Bi Lun (痹論) writes 'drinks much yet cannot get it out, the middle qi pants and struggles.' Here, taking 'cannot retain it within' (不得中) as the clause, this means it cannot be retained within, but comes out at once; I fear this is not the meaning of the classic.) At times there is onset of sunxie (飧泄). Now if one drinks frequently yet cannot retain it within, then the stool certainly will not be retained; in that case, wasting-thirst with frequent drinking and much urination is only because the dryness-heat of the three burners is depressed (怫鬱) and the qi declines—this is clear. How can one use drying-heat poisonous drugs to assist its strong yang and thereby attack the weak yin! This is truly the crime of making the excess more excessive and the deficiency more deficient (實實虛虛). Now in wasting-thirst, there are many transformations into deafness, blindness, sores, lichen, acne, and miliaria—all because the dryness-heat of the intestines and stomach is depressed, and the water and fluids cannot moisten and infiltrate the whole body.
translator_notes: 怫鬱 rendered 'depressed' with original characters; 飧泄 rendered 'sunxie'; 實實虛虛 kept as a technical phrase.
